citations.claim: energy increased after floor bounce despite e<1 and no controller work
first violating step energy exceeds allowed 4389.39, citation for violation
outgoing velocity larger than e*incoming suggests energy gain at bounce

counterfactual.change: Changed gravity from 14.451688623774244 to 0.0 only; energy then decreases 3214->3019 and no violation occurs, showing floor collision with gravity/substeps causes energy creation.

explanation: Energy increases without controller work. Body 1 hits floor between step0 and step1: incoming vy -45.26 with e=0.9 should rebound at ~40.7 but observed vy=+42.03, indicating restitution adds energy. With gravity=14.45 and 46 substeps, total mechanical energy rises from 3985 (step0) to 4217 (step1) to 4565 (step2) exceeding bound 4389. Setting gravity to 0 removes the excess, suggesting collision impulse and gravity integration in substeps interact to create energy.
vision_note: The lower body falls to the floor between step 0 and step 1, sitting at the bottom edge in frame 1, then visibly rebounds upward in frame 2 to a height that suggests excess energy. The upper body shows little motion, so the dominant event is the floor collision and the higher-than-expected bounce of the lower body.
